title: The Exact Prime-Degree Order and AGL(1,ℓ)
content: The parent chain squeezed |Gal(Xⁿ−p/ℚ)| between the metacyclic ceiling n·φ(n) and the lower bounds lcm(n,φ(n)) (always) and n·φ(n) (when gcd(n,φ(n))=1), pinning the order exactly at n·φ(n) in the coprime case. This file extracts the general prime-degree consequence: |Gal(Xˡ−p)| = ℓ(ℓ−1) = |AGL(1,ℓ)|, the order of the affine group 𝔽ₗ ⋊ 𝔽ₗˣ — the largest solvable transitive subgroup of Sₗ.

title: Prime Degree Supplies Coprimality for Free
content: coprime_self_totient_of_prime proves gcd(ℓ, φ(ℓ)) = 1 for prime ℓ. Since Nat.totient_prime gives φ(ℓ) = ℓ − 1, and a prime cannot divide a strictly smaller positive number, ℓ ∤ (ℓ − 1); Nat.Prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd converts non-divisibility to coprimality (omega closes it). This is exactly the hypothesis the parent's exact pin requires, supplied automatically at every prime degree.

title: The Exact Order |Gal(Xˡ−p)| = ℓ(ℓ−1)
content: gal_card_prime_degree is the headline: for every prime ℓ and prime p, |Gal(Xˡ−p/ℚ)| = ℓ(ℓ−1), with no genericity hypothesis and uniform in p. It applies the parent's coprime exact pin gal_card_eq_n_mul_totient_of_coprime — whose hypothesis is discharged by coprime_self_totient_of_prime — and rewrites φ(ℓ) = ℓ − 1. It subsumes the parent instances 2 (ℓ=2), 6 (ℓ=3), 20 (ℓ=5) in one statement.

title: Index (ℓ−2)! in Sₗ — Non-Genericity for ℓ ≥ 5
content: gal_index_in_symm proves |Gal(Xˡ−p)|·(ℓ−2)! = ℓ!, so Gal sits inside Sₗ with index exactly (ℓ−2)!. Writing ℓ = m+2, this is the factorisation ℓ! = ℓ(ℓ−1)(ℓ−2)! closed by ring. For ℓ ≥ 5 the index (ℓ−2)! > 1, so the Galois group of the irreducible separable Xˡ − p is a PROPER subgroup of Sₗ — radical polynomials are never Sₗ-generic at prime degree ≥ 5.

title: The Septic Instance |Gal(X⁷−p)| = 42
content: gal_card_septic_eq_42 specialises the closed form to ℓ = 7: |Gal(X⁷−p/ℚ)| = 42 = |AGL(1,7)| for every prime p, discharged by gal_card_prime_degree and norm_num. It is the next instance after the parent's quintic 20, and it dramatises how loose the factorial bound is — |Gal| ∣ 7! = 5040 cannot see 42 ≪ 5040.

title: Ceiling Meets Floor Forces Exact Equality
content: The exact order is not a fresh computation but a squeeze: the metacyclic ceiling |Gal| ≤ ℓ·φ(ℓ) and the coprime lower bound ℓ·φ(ℓ) ∣ |Gal| (available because gcd(ℓ,φ(ℓ)) = 1 at prime degree) sandwich the order at exactly ℓ·φ(ℓ). Divisibility upward plus boundedness downward by the same value is what upgrades a two-sided estimate into an equality.
prerequisites: antisymmetry of divisibility under a bound
